issues.description: Storing full credit card number in memory and interface definition. PCI-DSS compliance violation - card numbers should never be stored in application code.
issues.suggestion: Remove cardNumber from the interface. Use a payment gateway token or encrypted reference instead. Implement a secure payment processor (Stripe, Square, etc.) that handles card data and returns a token.

issues.description: Storing CVV in plain text. CVV must never be stored per PCI-DSS requirements - it should only be transmitted directly to payment processors.
issues.suggestion: Remove CVV from storage entirely. Pass card details directly to a PCI-compliant payment gateway without storing them. Use tokenization for recurring payments.

issues.description: Plain text validation of credit card details in application code. This requires the application to handle raw card data, violating PCI-DSS compliance.
issues.suggestion: Delegate all card validation to a PCI-compliant payment gateway. Use their SDK/API to tokenize card data on the client side before it reaches your server.

issues.description: Insufficient card number validation - only checks length. Does not validate card number format, checksum (Luhn algorithm), or card type.
issues.suggestion: If card validation is absolutely necessary (which it shouldn't be), implement Luhn algorithm validation and card type detection. Better: use a payment gateway's validation.

issues.description: Logging partial card numbers (last 4 digits) in database without encryption. While less sensitive, this still associates payments with partial card data.
issues.suggestion: Use payment gateway transaction IDs instead of card data. Store only the gateway's payment reference, amount, and status. Never store any card information.

issues.description: SQL query uses string interpolation pattern that could be vulnerable if db.query doesn't properly parameterize. No visible SQL injection protection verification.
issues.suggestion: Verify that db.query properly handles parameterized queries. Add explicit documentation that $1, $2, etc. are parameterized. Consider using an ORM (Prisma, TypeORM) for type-safe queries.

issues.description: SQL query concatenates JSON.stringify output directly into query without validation. If db.query doesn't escape properly, this could allow injection.
issues.suggestion: Use JSONB column type with proper parameterization. Pass features array as a parameter and let the database driver handle serialization: db.query(query, [userId, tier, validUntil, features]).

issues.description: No error handling around database query. Database errors could expose subscription status or SQL structure to callers.
issues.suggestion: Wrap database calls in try-catch blocks. Return false on error without exposing database details. Log errors securely for monitoring.

issues.description: Error thrown for invalid payment details doesn't clean up or log transaction attempt. Could lose track of failed payment attempts.
issues.suggestion: Log all payment attempts (successful and failed) with transaction IDs for audit trail. Return structured error objects instead of throwing, allowing caller to handle gracefully.

issues.description: Date comparison uses current time but doesn't account for timezone differences. Card expiry is end-of-month, not exact date.
issues.suggestion: Set expiry date to last day of the month at 23:59:59 UTC. Use date-fns or dayjs library for reliable date handling: endOfMonth(new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month) - 1)).

issues.description: Calculates price on every call with floating-point arithmetic. Could lead to rounding errors in financial calculations.
issues.suggestion: Pre-calculate prices and store in a constant lookup table. Use integer arithmetic (cents) for all monetary calculations to avoid floating-point errors. Return Math.round(total * 100) / 100.

issues.description: Payment processing catches errors but only logs to console. In production, this error would be lost and payment status unclear.
issues.suggestion: Implement proper error logging with a service (Sentry, LogRocket). Store failed payment attempts in database with error details. Alert on payment failures for investigation.

issues.description: No rollback mechanism if upgradeUserSubscription fails after chargeCard succeeds. Customer charged but subscription not upgraded.
issues.suggestion: Implement database transaction wrapping both operations. If upgrade fails, refund the charge. Consider using a state machine or saga pattern for payment workflows.

issues.description: Hardcoded feature lists duplicated for each tier. Adding features requires code changes and deployment.
issues.suggestion: Extract features to a configuration file or database table. Use a tier configuration object: const TIER_FEATURES = { premium: [...], enterprise: [...] }. Better: store in database for dynamic updates.

issues.description: Magic numbers for tax rate and processing fee hardcoded without explanation or configuration.
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch. Validate parsed data structure. Consider using Zod schema validation: const featuresSchema = z.array(z.string()); featuresSchema.parse(JSON.parse(subscription.features)).

issues.description: Expired subscriptions checked in application code but user still exists in database. No automated cleanup of expired subscriptions.
issues.suggestion: Implement a background job to clean up or mark expired subscriptions. Add a database constraint or index on valid_until for efficient queries. Consider adding a status column.

issues.description: Database query returns all columns with SELECT * when only specific fields are needed.
issues.suggestion: Select only required columns: SELECT user_id, tier, valid_until, features FROM subscriptions WHERE user_id = $1. Reduces data transfer and parsing overhead.

issues.description: Expiry date parsing uses parseInt without validation. Invalid input could cause NaN or incorrect date calculations.
issues.suggestion: Validate parsed integers are valid numbers: const month = parseInt(monthStr, 10); if (isNaN(month) || month < 1 || month > 12) return false;. Use regex groups to extract and validate in one step.

issues.description: No input sanitization or validation for userId. Could accept malicious input leading to SQL injection or data corruption.
issues.suggestion: Validate userId format (UUID, integer, etc.) before use. Use a validation library like Zod: z.string().uuid().parse(userId). Reject invalid input early.

issues.description: Function chargeCard simulates payment gateway but has no actual integration. Misleading function name suggests real payment processing.
issues.suggestion: Rename to simulatePayment() or implement actual payment gateway integration (Stripe SDK). Add TODO comments if this is placeholder code. Throw error in production if not implemented.

issues.description: Calculates validUntil date on every subscription creation. Simple calculation but could be extracted for reusability.
issues.suggestion: Create a helper function getSubscriptionEndDate(startDate: Date, durationMonths: number). Makes it easier to offer different subscription lengths (monthly, yearly).

issues.description: Entire payment processing module has no test coverage as noted in comments. Critical business logic handling payments is untested.
issues.suggestion: Implement comprehensive unit tests for all functions, especially payment validation, pricing calculations, and subscription upgrades. Use test doubles for database. Aim for 100% coverage on payment logic.

issues.description: No validation that tier parameter matches intended subscription level. Could potentially allow price manipulation.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (!['premium', 'enterprise'].includes(tier)) throw new Error('Invalid tier'). Consider using TypeScript literal types more strictly.

issues.description: Creates new Date() object twice for expiration check - once on line 157, once on line 160. Inefficient.
issues.suggestion: Create once and reuse: const now = new Date(); if (validUntil < now) return false;

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUES: This code has severe PCI-DSS compliance violations that make it unsuitable for production use. It stores and processes raw credit card data (card numbers and CVV) in application code, which violates payment card industry security standards. The code must be completely refactored to use a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, Square, Braintree) that handles all card data through tokenization. Additional critical issues include: potential SQL injection vulnerabilities, lack of error handling in payment processing, no transaction rollback mechanism, and zero test coverage for critical payment logic. The code also has maintainability issues with hardcoded pricing and features. Immediate action required: Do not deploy this code to production. Implement proper payment gateway integration, add comprehensive test coverage, and ensure all financial calculations use integer arithmetic.

untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that payment.amount less than calculated tier price throws 'Insufficient payment amount' error

untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that card numbers with length != 16 (too short: 15 digits, too long: 17 digits) return false

untestedPaths.reasoning: CVV validation accepting both 3 and 4 digit codes (Visa/MC vs Amex). Incorrect logic could reject legitimate cards or accept invalid CVVs.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that CVV with 3 digits returns true, CVV with 4 digits returns true, CVV with 2 or 5+ digits returns false

untestedPaths.reasoning: Regex validation for MM/YY format. Invalid format checking could allow malformed dates through processing pipeline.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test valid format '12/25' returns true, invalid formats '13/25' (bad month), '1/25' (single digit month), '12/2025' (four digit year) return false

untestedPaths.reasoning: CONTAINS SYNTAX ERROR - code is truncated at 'if (e'. This prevents compilation. After fixing, must verify expired cards are rejected while valid future dates are accepted.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: After fixing syntax error, test that expiry date in the past returns false, current month returns true, future date returns true

untestedPaths.reasoning: Calculates final charge amount including tax and fees. Errors in pricing calculation directly impact revenue - overcharging damages customer trust, undercharging causes revenue loss. Complex calculation with multiple components requires thorough testing.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier returns correct total including base price, 8% tax, and 2.9% processing fee; enterprise tier calculates correctly with same formula

untestedPaths.reasoning: Executes actual payment charge via database insertion. Simulates payment gateway interaction. No tests verify successful charges, database failures, or proper error handling. A bug could result in lost transactions or incorrect payment records.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test successful charge inserts correct record with last 4 digits, amount, and 'completed' status, then returns true

untestedPaths.reasoning: Catch block handles database/payment failures. Without tests, cannot verify failures return false instead of throwing, and that errors are properly logged.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that database query failure is caught, error is logged, and function returns false instead of throwing

untestedPaths.reasoning: Grants subscription access and features. No tests verify correct tier assignment, feature sets, or date calculations. Bugs could grant wrong features or incorrect subscription duration.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier sets features ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'] with valid_until = current date + 1 year

untestedPaths.reasoning: Different feature sets for premium vs enterprise. Must verify each tier grants exactly the correct features - no more, no less.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test enterprise tier sets all 5 features including 'api_access' and 'team_collaboration', premium tier sets only first 3 features

untestedPaths.reasoning: Boundary condition where payment.amount exactly equals calculated price. Should be explicitly tested to ensure >= comparison works correctly at the boundary.

untestedPaths.reasoning: If upgradeUserSubscription fails after successful payment, customer is charged but not upgraded. This creates a critical inconsistency requiring proper error handling or transaction management.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Boundary condition for cards expiring in the current month. The expiry date logic creates a Date object with the expiry month/year, but cards typically expire at the END of the month shown. The comparison may incorrectly reject cards valid for the current month.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that a card expiring in the current month (e.g., if today is 05/15/2025, expiry '05/25') is treated as valid

untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that calculated amounts are correctly rounded to 2 decimal places for currency representation

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL: Zero test coverage exists for payment processing code in src/premium.ts. All 7 functions are completely untested, including business-critical payment flow (processPremiumPayment), card validation (validatePaymentDetails), pricing calculations (calculateSubscriptionPrice), payment execution (chargeCard), subscription management (upgradeUserSubscription), and access control (hasFeatureAccess, getUserSubscription). The file contains 15 critical-priority gaps, 13 high-priority gaps, and 7 medium-priority gaps. Additionally, a syntax error exists on line 88 that prevents compilation. Immediate action required: (1) Fix syntax error, (2) Add comprehensive test suite covering all payment flows, validation logic, error paths, and edge cases, (3) Implement integration tests for payment transaction atomicity, (4) Add tests for database error handling and rollback scenarios. This code should not be deployed to production without thorough test coverage due to financial, security, and compliance risks.

refactorings.summary: The src/premium.ts file contains critical payment processing logic that would benefit significantly from refactoring. The main issues are: (1) High-impact opportunities - Feature configuration extraction, pricing constant extraction, and database query consolidation will dramatically improve maintainability and reduce risk. (2) Medium-impact opportunities - Date handling functions, validation logic extraction, and subscription checking simplification will improve testability and code clarity. (3) Low-impact opportunities - Variable renaming, error message constants, and simplified boolean logic will improve readability. Priority actions: Start with high-impact refactorings (feature configuration, pricing constants, query builders) as these affect critical business logic and have the highest risk of bugs. Then address medium-impact items to improve testability, which is crucial given the complete lack of tests for this payment processing code. All refactorings preserve existing behavior while improving structure, testability, and maintainability.

recommendations.description: Immediately remove all credit card data handling from application code. Integrate with a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, Square, Braintree) that handles card tokenization. Never store card numbers, CVV, or raw payment data in your application.

Add comprehensive test suite for all payment processing functions. Priority: processPremiumPayment, validatePaymentDetails, calculateSubscriptionPrice, chargeCard, and upgradeUserSubscription. Include unit tests, integration tests, and tests for all error paths and edge cases.
Fix syntax error on line 88 in validatePaymentDetails function where code is truncated at 'if (e'. This prevents compilation and must be fixed before deployment.

Verify all database queries use proper parameterization. Replace JSON.stringify inline concatenation with parameterized JSONB handling. Consider using an ORM (Prisma, TypeORM) for type-safe, injection-proof queries.

Implement database transactions wrapping payment charge and subscription upgrade operations. Add rollback mechanism to refund charges if subscription upgrade fails. Consider using a saga pattern for complex payment workflows.

Replace floating-point arithmetic with integer arithmetic (cents) for all monetary calculations. Pre-calculate prices and store in constants. Add proper rounding to prevent precision errors that could result in incorrect charges.

Implement proper error logging service (Sentry, LogRocket) to replace console.error. Store all payment attempts (successful and failed) in database with audit trail. Add monitoring alerts for payment failures.

Add comprehensive input validation for userId, payment amounts, and tier parameters. Use validation library like Zod to enforce type safety and prevent malicious input. Validate all external inputs before processing.

Extract hardcoded feature lists, pricing constants, tax rates, and processing fees into configuration objects. This enables easier updates, better testability, and supports future dynamic pricing strategies.

Centralize all SQL queries into a QUERIES constant object and extract database operations into dedicated functions (recordPayment, upsertSubscription, etc.). Improves maintainability, security review, and testability.

Extract date parsing and comparison logic into dedicated functions (parseExpiryDate, isCardExpired, isSubscriptionExpired). Use a date library (date-fns, dayjs) for reliable timezone handling and end-of-month calculations.
Extract individual validation rules into separate functions (isValidCardNumber, isValidCVV, isValidExpiryFormat). Makes each validation independently testable and improves code modularity.
